question: Manisha bought a toy for ₹940, decorated it at a cost of ₹10 and sold the toy for ₹659. Find the loss or profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total CP = Purchase Price + Decoration Cost = 940 + 10 = ₹950

Loss = Total CP − SP = 950 − 659 = ₹291

Loss % = (Loss ÷ Total CP) × 100

Loss % = (291 ÷ 950) × 100 = 582/19 % loss

**∴ The correct answer is 582/19 % loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Purchase price of the toy = ₹940

Cost of decoration = ₹10

Selling price (SP) of the toy = ₹659

**Formula Used:**

Total Cost Price (CP) = Purchase Price + Overhead Expenses

Loss = Total CP − SP

Loss % = (Loss ÷ Total CP) × 100

 Profit & Loss Breakdown
 
 
 
 
 SP = ₹659
 Loss = ₹291

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) = 940 + 10 = ₹950

⇒ Since Total CP > SP, there is a loss on the transaction.

⇒ Loss = 950 − 659 = ₹291

⇒ Loss % = (291 ÷ 950) × 100

⇒ Loss % = 2910 ÷ 95

⇒ Loss % = 582/19 %

**∴ The correct answer is 582/19 % loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Overhead Expenses

Any additional costs incurred before the sale of an item, such as transportation, repair, or decoration, are always added to the base purchase price to form the Total Cost Price.

Profit and Loss Formulation

Profit occurs when SP > CP and Loss occurs when CP > SP. Both Profit % and Loss % are always calculated based on the Total Cost Price unless specifically stated otherwise.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always applied on the Marked Price (MP). It is deduced before calculating profit or loss. Formula: SP = MP − Discount.
